en.text: Now when the wall was built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed,

zhSimplified.text: 城墙修完，我安了门扇，守门的、歌唱的，和利未人都已派定。

zhTraditional.text: 城牆修完，我安了門扇，守門的、歌唱的，和利未人都已派定。

en.text: I put my brother Hanani, and Hananiah the governor of the fortress, in charge of Jerusalem; for he was a faithful man and feared God above many.

zhSimplified.text: 我就派我的弟兄哈拿尼和营楼的宰官哈拿尼雅管理耶路撒冷；因为哈拿尼雅是忠信的，又敬畏 神过于众人。

zhTraditional.text: 我就派我的弟兄哈拿尼和營樓的宰官哈拿尼雅管理耶路撒冷；因為哈拿尼雅是忠信的，又敬畏上帝過於眾人。

en.text: I said to them, “Don’t let the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun is hot; and while they stand guard, let them shut the doors, and you bar them; and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, everyone in his watch, with everyone near his house.”

zhSimplified.text: 我吩咐他们说：「等到太阳上升才可开耶路撒冷的城门；人尚看守的时候就要关门上闩；也当派耶路撒冷的居民各按班次看守自己房屋对面之处。」 （拉2·1—70）

zhTraditional.text: 我吩咐他們說：「等到太陽上升才可開耶路撒冷的城門；人尚看守的時候就要關門上閂；也當派耶路撒冷的居民各按班次看守自己房屋對面之處。」 （拉2‧1－70）

en.text: Now the city was wide and large; but the people were few therein, and the houses were not built.

zhSimplified.text: 城是广大，其中的民却稀少，房屋还没有建造。

zhTraditional.text: 城是廣大，其中的民卻稀少，房屋還沒有建造。

en.text: My God put into my heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that they might be listed by genealogy. I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found this written in it:

zhSimplified.text: 我的 神感动我心，招聚贵胄、官长，和百姓，要照家谱计算。我找着第一次上来之人的家谱，其上写着：

zhTraditional.text: 我的上帝感動我心，招聚貴冑、官長，和百姓，要照家譜計算。我找着第一次上來之人的家譜，其上寫着：

en.text: These are the children of the province who went up out of the captivity of those who had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, everyone to his city,

zhSimplified.text: 巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒从前掳去犹大省的人，现在他们的子孙从被掳到之地回耶路撒冷和犹大，各归本城。

en.text: Some from among the heads of fathers’ households gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand darics of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred thirty priests’ garments.

footnotes.text: 7:70 a daric was a gold coin issued by a Persian king, weighing about 8.4 grams or about 0.27 troy ounces each.

zhSimplified.text: 有些族长为工程捐助。省长捐入库中的金子一千达利克，碗五十个，祭司的礼服五百三十件。

en.text: Some of the heads of fathers’ households gave into the treasury of the work twenty thousand darics of gold, and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.

footnotes.text: 7:71 A mina is about 600 grams or 1.3 U. S. pounds, so 2,200 minas is about 1.3 metric tons.

zhSimplified.text: 又有族长捐入工程库的金子二万达利克，银子二千二百弥拿。

zhTraditional.text: 又有族長捐入工程庫的金子二萬達利克，銀子二千二百彌拿。

en.text: That which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand darics of gold, plus two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests’ garments.

zhSimplified.text: 其余百姓所捐的金子二万达利克，银子二千弥拿，祭司的礼服六十七件。

zhTraditional.text: 其餘百姓所捐的金子二萬達利克，銀子二千彌拿，祭司的禮服六十七件。

en.text: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel lived in their cities.

zhSimplified.text: 于是祭司、利未人、守门的、歌唱的、民中的一些人、尼提宁，并以色列众人，各住在自己的城里。

zhTraditional.text: 於是祭司、利未人、守門的、歌唱的、民中的一些人、尼提寧，並以色列眾人，各住在自己的城裏。
